The .sav variable labels tie all 12 codes to form q.5.3 options 01-12 by number and content, 12/12 (I5301. Como se siente  Ud. en la casa; I5302 En el trabajo; ... I5308. een el automovil [label typo]; I5310. En los parques; I5311. En los centros de diversion; I5312. En los espectaculos). Words are the official Spanish questionnaire p.5 (section V. PERCEPCION DE LA INSEGURIDAD PUBLICA), checked against the rendered page image, not the terse .sav labels. q.5.3 has one shared stem, so instructions joins the form scale line and the stem with one space, no punctuation added (as in sibling ecuador_2011_safety_confidence): En una escala de 1 a 5, donde significa: “1” Muy inseguro y “5” Muy seguro ¿Cómo se siente usted en ...; each location phrase is item_text as printed, including the leading en the form prints on options 10-12, the form space before each closing ? (none on el transporte público?), and the small-italic examples (Ej. discoteca), (Ej. conciertos, estadio, etc.); accents as printed; single section; interviewer line ANOTE EL CODIGO CORRESPONDIENTE PARA CADA OPCION (RM) not shipped. Options: the form labels only the endpoints (1 Muy inseguro, 5 Muy seguro, in both the scale line and the 1-5 box row), so resp 2-4 have blank option_text. The .sav value labels do name every point (1 Muy inseguro, 2 Inseguro, 3 Ni seguro  ni  inseguro [double spaces in the label], 4 Seguro, 5 Muy seguro, 7 No aplica, 8 No sabe, 9 no responde) and the do-file maps those strings to 1-5 and drops 7/8/9; those intermediate labels are the data file's coding, not wording printed for the respondent, so they are not shipped as option_text (recorded in public_note). Route 9 by server-side GROUP BY (no export): live item x resp counts equal .sav counts in 60/60 cells, and the 12 count vectors are mutually distinct (e.g. I5301 7826/14554/33284/36144/25812; I5307 33583/36666/24515/11212/3889); dropped No aplica/No sabe/No responde per item range 117 (I5301) to 86079 (I5303). public_note: The English in the _translated columns is an IRW machine translation of the Spanish INEC questionnaire; the questionnaire labels only scale points 1 (Muy inseguro) and 5 (Muy seguro), so points 2-4 have no option text, although the INEC data file labels them Inseguro, Ni seguro ni inseguro and Seguro.
